questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'abundant':
questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities; plentiful. Its opposite is scarce.

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'benevolent':
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning, kindly, charitable.

questions.question: Choose the opposite (antonym) of 'transparent':
questions.explanation: Transparent means see-through. Opaque means not able to be seen through — its direct opposite.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.explanation: The correct form for third person singular present tense is 'doesn't' (does not) followed by the base verb 'have'.

questions.question: Identify the correct passive form of: 'The boy ate the mango.'
options: The mango was eaten by the boy
The mango is eaten by the boy
The mango has ate by the boy
questions.explanation: The past tense 'ate' becomes 'was eaten' in passive voice. Object becomes subject: The mango was eaten by the boy.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
questions.explanation: Direct questions end with a question mark, and a name in direct address is set off by a comma.

questions.question: The plural of 'crisis' is:
questions.explanation: Crisis is from Greek; its plural is crises (change of -is to -es).

questions.question: 'He kicked the bucket' is an example of:
questions.explanation: This is an idiom meaning 'he died'. It cannot be understood from the individual meanings of the words.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is: 'She is as busy as a bee'?
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'. This compares her busyness to a bee's.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is: 'The wind whispered through the trees'?
questions.explanation: Personification gives human qualities (whispering) to non-human things (wind).

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'frugal':
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful with money, economical, thrifty.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'If I ______ a bird, I would fly south.'
questions.explanation: This is a second conditional sentence (unreal present). The subjunctive 'were' is used for all subjects.

questions.question: 'The sun ______ in the east.' Choose the correct verb form:
questions.explanation: This is a general truth/habitual action, so simple present tense is used. 'The sun' is third person singular, so 'rises'.

questions.question: A synonym for 'diligent' is:
questions.explanation: Diligent means showing careful and persistent effort; hardworking.

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'obstinate':
questions.explanation: Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion; unyielding.

questions.question: Identify the correct reported speech: He said, 'I am going to school now.'
options: He said that he is going to school now
He said that he was going to school then
He said that he went to school now
He said that I was going to school
questions.explanation: In reported speech: 'am going' → 'was going', 'now' → 'then', and first person 'I' → third person 'he'.

questions.question: 'His speech was a breath of fresh air' is:
questions.explanation: 'A breath of fresh air' is an idiom meaning something new and refreshing, different from what came before.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a relative pronoun?
options: The book that I read was interesting
questions.explanation: 'That' is a relative pronoun introducing the relative clause 'that I read'.

questions.question: The word 'meticulous' means:
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.

questions.question: Which sentence is a paradox?
options: She is as tall as a building
I must be cruel to be kind
The classroom was as quiet as a graveyard
questions.explanation: A paradox is a statement that appears self-contradictory but may reveal a truth. 'Cruel to be kind' seems contradictory.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: Me and him went to school
He and I went to school
Him and me went to school
I and he went to school
questions.explanation: Subject pronouns (he, I) are used as subjects. Also, etiquette places 'I' last when referring to yourself with another person.

questions.question: A word that is spelled the same but has different meanings (e.g., 'bat') is called:
questions.explanation: A homonym has the same spelling but different meanings (bat = animal, bat = sports equipment). Homophones sound the same but may be spelled differently.

questions.question: 'Many hands make light work' is best described as:
questions.explanation: A proverb is a short saying expressing a general truth or piece of advice. This teaches that cooperation makes tasks easier.

questions.question: The passive voice of: 'The teacher will punish the students.'
options: The students will be punished by the teacher
The students were punished by the teacher
The students are punished by the teacher
The students would punish the teacher
questions.explanation: Future tense 'will punish' becomes 'will be punished' in passive voice.

questions.question: The antonym of 'benevolent' is:
questions.explanation: Malevolent means wishing harm to others — the direct opposite of benevolent (wishing good for others).
